detail.title: Path Dependence in Multi-Agent Interaction Protocols
detail.summary: This synthesis evaluates how initial communication constraints in MARL systems function as structural precursors, guiding the trajectory of emergent social dynamics. By projecting existing communicative MARL (Comm-MADRL) approaches into a multidimensional space, this research highlights that interaction protocols are not merely operational settings but critical determinants of long-term preference stability.
detail.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence analysis regarding MARL communication architectures.

children.title: Cycle 39 · Synthesis of Path Dependence and Value Alignment in Multi-Agent Systems

detail.title: Synthesis of Path Dependence and Value Alignment in Multi-Agent Systems
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on path dependence in emergent agent preferences and the formalization of value system learning. Recent work clarifies that communication protocols and initial architectural constraints in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) significantly influence long-term preference emergence, while game-theoretic integrations provide necessary rigor for aligning agent objectives with human value systems.
